title: One tiger picture in five sizes
description: Shows one tiger picture resized into five copies: three keep the look of the tiger, one is stretched and one is squashed.

title: Same factor keeps the shape
description: Shows that halving both sides of a 60 mm by 40 mm picture keeps its shape, while taking 20 mm off both sides stretches it.

title: Image A grows to image D by one factor
description: Shows that both the width and the height of image A are multiplied by 3/2 to give image D, so the change is proportional.

title: Two equal factors, one shape
description: Shows the simplest resize: a 3 by 2 rectangle with width and height both multiplied by 2 becomes a 6 by 4 rectangle of the same shape.

title: Width to height is 60 : 40
description: Shows the ratio of width to height of image A as 60 : 40, with its two terms in order.

title: Both reduce to 3 : 2
description: Shows that 60 : 40 and 90 : 60 reduce to the same simplest form 3 : 2, so they are in proportion.

title: 72 : 96 reduces to 3 : 4
description: Shows 72 : 96 reduced by its HCF 24 to 3 : 4, so 3 : 4 and 72 : 96 are in proportion.

title: Which coffee is strongest?
description: Shows three 50 mL coffees as decoction and milk layers so the ratios 1 : 4, 3 : 7 and 2 : 3 can be compared by eye.

title: Mixing regular coffee: 15 : 35 is 3 : 7
description: Shows the ratio mixer in its simplest state: 15 mL of decoction and 35 mL of milk poured into one cup, with the ratio and its simplest form.

title: One factor for both terms
description: Shows 14 : 21 becoming 6 : 9 when both terms are multiplied by the same fractional factor 3/7.

title: 6 : 10 :: 18 : 30 for the lemonade
description: Shows glasses and spoons both multiplied by 3, keeping the lemonade equally sweet.

title: Equally strong walls
description: Shows that a 60 ft wall with 3 bags and a 40 ft wall with 2 bags both use one bag for every 20 ft.

title: Fill the missing term with one factor
description: Shows the ratio table in its simplest state: 4 : 9 scaled by 3 to fill the missing term 27.

title: Rule of Three: the mid-day meal
description: Shows 120 students needing 15 kg of rice and 80 students needing 10 kg, with one factor 2/3 applied to both.

title: Cross multiplication: ad = bc
description: Shows that in 120 : 15 :: 80 : 10 the outer terms and the inner terms give the same product.

title: Same units first
description: Shows that once 4 hours is written as 240 minutes, 150 minutes : 90 km and 240 minutes : 144 km line up on a double number line.

title: Two number lines that stretch together
description: Shows the double number line in its simplest state: 500 mL fills in 15 seconds, so 10000 mL fills in 300 seconds.

title: Adding years changes the ratio
description: Compares Neelima's and her mother's ages now (3 and 30) and 9 years later (12 and 39) to show the ratio changes.

title: Faster speed, less time
description: Before and after: the same 100 km trip takes 2 hours at 50 km/h but only 1 h 20 min at 75 km/h, not 3 hours.

title: Adding change or multiplying change?
description: Shows the sorting move of the practice: an age pair 1 : 5 that grows by adding 3 to each goes into the adding change bin.

title: Compare the price of 1 kg
description: Shows five 200 g packets making 1 kg for ₹1000 beside one 1 kg packet for ₹800, so the first tea is dearer.

title: Price per mL
description: Shows four shampoo sizes with their prices and the price of one mL, which is not proportional to volume.

title: Which city is more crowded?
description: Shows the unit rate finder in its simplest state: people per sq. km in Delhi and Mumbai, drawn as dots in areas.

title: Sharing 42 in the ratio 4 : 3
description: Shows 42 counters arranged as 7 groups of 6, with 4 groups for the partner and 3 for you.

title: Sharing ₹4000 in the ratio 3 : 1
description: Shows a profit of ₹4000 split into 4 equal groups of 1000, three for Prashanti and one for Bhuvan.

title: Adding cement to change the ratio
description: Compares a 40 kg mixture of 30 kg sand and 10 kg cement (3 : 1) with the mixture after adding 2 kg of cement (30 : 12, which is 5 : 2).

title: Split the bar into 2 + 3 groups
description: Shows the ratio sharer in its simplest state: ₹4500 cut into 5 equal groups of 900, two for one part and three for the other.

title: Hectares to acres
description: Shows the conversion 1 hectare = 2.471 acres used as a proportion to turn 2 hectares into 4.942 acres.

title: Celsius and Fahrenheit side by side
description: Shows that 0 °C sits at 32 °F and 25 °C at 77 °F, so Fahrenheit is 9/5 times Celsius plus 32, not a simple ratio.

title: Convert, then reason
description: Shows a 200 ft by 500 ft plot being converted to acres before finding the tonnes of manure.

title: Three big ideas about proportion
description: Summarises the chapter in three cards: a ratio a : b, a proportion with ad = bc, and sharing in the ratio m : n.

title: Filling a Binairo row
description: Shows a 6 cell Binairo row with three given symbols and three found by the rules: H H V H V V.
